intent: The capital nobody files under cold: three cold-country flags, one answer with a sub-zero yearly average, the altitude that explains it, and the fact that half a nation lives in it.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where is the COLDEST capital city on Earth?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Where is the coldest capital city on Earth?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Mongolia. Ulaanbaatar is the only capital on Earth whose average temperature, over the whole year, is below freezing.

lines.direction: the night counter drops to −30 on 'January'; pull back west so Kazakhstan shares the frame, it lights dim with the Astana pin and tag; a shrug sticker on 'Ottawa'
lines.text: January nights there pass minus 30. Astana, in Kazakhstan, is second; Ottawa is not close.

lines.direction: push in on the city; the altitude counter climbs to 1,350 and the mountain sticker lands on 'height'; the tag on 'metres'; a pulse on 'ocean'
lines.text: The secret is height: the city sits over 1,300 metres up, on a plateau far from any ocean.

lines.direction: settle on the country; the HALF THE NATION card on 'half', people sticker on 'million', a last pulse and the cool flag-ball on 'valley'
lines.text: And about half of all Mongolians live in it, more than 1,600,000 people in a single cold valley.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Colder than you thought. Follow us.
